HLB Options

AMC25.40.025 (F)(2):
 Heritage Land Bank land may be leased non-
competitively to a non-profit agency for less than its
appraised fair market value if the municipal benefits which
are projected to accrue are found by the mayor and the
assembly to be in the best interest of the municipality.



AMC 25.40.025(H)
In order to assist development that  will provide public
benefits and notwithstanding any other provision of this
section, Heritage Land Bank land may be disposed of by
lease,  sale  or  other  disposition,  for  the  purpose  of
facilitating a specific project. The project shall provide public
benefits. In addition to and consistent with the applicable
requirements of  titles 21, 23 and 24 of this Code, the
disposition  shall  include  additional  requirements  and
conditions   to  insure  the  proper  development  and
completion of the project in the public interest. Disposals
pursuant to this subsection shall be through requests for
proposals or through invitations to bid. The disposition of
property pursuant to this subsection may be for less than
fair market value or less than  fair market  rental  rate.
However, the Heritage Land Bank shall, for informational
purposes only:

1. Provide a descriptive summary of the public benefits
expected from the project; and

2. Obtain an appraisal of the value of the property,
determined by a certified real estate appraiser, if it were
disposed of without the development requirements
imposed pursuant to this subsection. Assembly approval
of a disposition under this subsection shall include a
finding that the disposition provides public benefits.

3. A summary listing and description of estimated
economic and non-economic benefits and costs
associated with the project. This summary should be
succinct, concise, and quantified where appropriate, and
should not exceed two pages in length.

GIRDWOOD PROPERTY TAX INCENTIVE PROGRAM


Program 1 STR to LTR Conversion

1. Provide an exemption from property tax for property owners who convert a property or
an ADU located in the Girdwood Valley Service Area from a short term rental to a long term
rental. This exemption would have the following characteristics:

       a. Eligibility- Property owner must have previously registered the property for which
an exemption is sought as an STR.

       b. Proof of Conversion- Property owner must submit copy of long term lease with
the lease term starting no later than January 1 of the year for which an exemption is
requested.

        c. Full Year LTR Required- Property owner must commit to maintaining property as
a long term lease through December 31 of the year for which an exemption is requested.

       d. Primary Residence- Tenant must use property as primary residence.

        e. Application- MOA to provide application form. Application to be submitted by
existing deadline for other property tax exemption applications (Senior Citizen, Primary
Residence etc.).

           f. Renewal- Unlike other exemptions property owner must provide proof of
continuing LTR use of the property for which an exemption has been granted by an annual
deadline date. Done using annual certiﬁcate of eligibility ﬁled by Feb. 1 (see AMC
12.35.020) or March 15 (see AMC 12.15.015( C)(4).

        g. Deﬁnition- deﬁnition of Long Term Rental and Short Term Rental matches state
exemption statute - month to month lease period qualiﬁes as LTR. STR dos not include
hotel, motel or bed and breakfast.

        g. Scope of Exemption- Only applies to the Girdwood Valley Service Area
component of MOA property taxes. [i.e. partial exemption].

      For ADU exemption is pro rata based on size of ADU.

       h. Amount and Length of Exemption- TBD but starting point for discussion:

               a. Length- 10 years

               b. Amount- 100% in Year 1 and then declines 10% per year

i. Ordinance Sunsets After 5 years- allows opportunity to see if program is working

           j. Annual reporting


     Program 2 - Add Girdwood Valley Service Area to AMC 12.60.010

              This is an existing code provision exempting 8 unit multi-family
developments from property tax for 20 years. The exemption period can be expanded for 5
years in a deﬁned “Residential Housing Tax Incentive Area. Girdwood Valley Service Area is
not currently included in the Tax incentive area.


     Program 3- Workforce Housing Property Tax Exemption

       1. Amend state law (AS 29.45.050 ) similar to what was done last legislative session
by adding a new optional exemption to read similar to the following:

          (ff) A municipality may by ordinance partially exempt from taxation a workforce
housing property for a period not to exceed ﬁfteen years. However, a municipality that is a
school district may only exempt all or a portion of the amount of taxes that exceeds the
amount levied on other property for the school district. In this subsection “workforce
housing property” means real property that: [GHEC to discuss deﬁnition]


NOTE: likely need to limit this to property managed/owned by a community land trust or
nonproﬁt housing development entity.


     Program 4 – Low Income Rental Property Exemption

       1. Anchorage has the authority to adopt such an exemption. AS 29.45.050(cc).
Note: low income uses federal deﬁnition based on average AGI. Rent charged cannot
exceed 30% of family’s income. Could be a partial exemption.

WHEREAS, as a resort community, Girdwood faces high external housing demand and has
seen a drastic increase in short term rentals in the last 10 years, making it challenging for
year-round residents of Girdwood to obtain housing, and raising concerns among residents
that the character of this beloved and close-knit community will be lost as community
members, especially working and middle class families, will be increasingly priced out of
the housing market; and


WHEREAS, to meet the workforce housing needs in Girdwood, the development of housing
that is at least 50% occupied as primary residences whether owner occupied or leased on
a ﬁve-month to yearly basis should be prioritized; and


WHEREAS, there is an immediate need for 75 units of workforce housing to address current
workforce demand for housing (GAP p. 2-47) ; and


WHEREAS, the Girdwood community seeks some relief to the housing pressures
experienced by current and future full-time residents of Girdwood, speciﬁcally by providing
more stable long-term rental property and more attainable housing to those at 120 percent
and below area median incomes; and

WHEREAS, Policy H1.3 of the Girdwood Comprehensive Plan is to “Encourage long-term
rentals by providing incentives such as using tax incentives or exemptions for property-
owners.” (GAP p. 4-8) and

WHEREAS, the “Implementation Action” identiﬁed for Policy H1.3 is to “Develop an
incentive tax structure for long-term rentals. Work with state legislators to amend any
necessary state-level policies related to this goal.” And

WHEREAS, GBOS is identiﬁed as one of the “implementers/partners” for Policy H1.3
policy; and

WHEREAS, in 2026 the Alaska Legislature amended AS 29.45.050 which established
authority for the Municipality of Anchorage to provide full or partial exemptions from
municipal property tax for properties:

       a. converted from short term rentals to long term rentals;

       b. property rented to a low income family and

        c. property owned and occupied by a ﬁrst time home buyer

WHEREAS, Goal H4.4 of the GAP is to “Develop an appropriate property tax incentive
program to implement in Girdwood.” (GAP p. 4-11) and

WHEREAS, GBOS is identiﬁed as one of the “implementers/partners” for Policy H4.4 policy
together with the MOA Finance Department;

The Girdwood Housing and Economic Committee recommends the Girdwood Board of
Supervisors do the following:

1. Adopt the attached Girdwood Property Tax Incentive Program.

2. Inform MOA officials at the next GBOS-MOA quarterly meeting that GBOS has adopted
the Girdwood Property Tax Incentive Program and request MOA Finance identify a person to
work with GBOS and Girdwood’s Assembly representative to prepare an ordinance
providing property tax incentives for properties converted from short term to long term
rentals.

3. Ask Girdwood’s Assembly representatives to add the Girdwood Valley Service Area to
the Residential housing tax incentive area deﬁned in AMC 12.60.080. (this is a multi-family
development exemption).

4. Inform state elected officials representing Girdwood that GBOS has adopted the
Girdwood Property Tax Incentive Program and request those official to identify staff to work
with GBOS to prepare a proposed state law that would authorize Alaskan municipalities to
enact a whole or partial property tax exemption for the development of new units of
workforce housing that are managed by a community land trust or nonproﬁt affordable
homeownership developers.

5. Support the proposed Anchorage ordinance providing an exemption for ﬁrst time home
buyers.

6. Ask the Mayor’s Office to prepare an ordinance exempting or partially exempting real
property rented to a low income family if the rent charged is not more than 30% of that
family’s income.

Recommended Girdwood Workforce Housing Deﬁnition for GHEC Consideration


Primary Policy Objective:

Preserving housing for people who work in and sustain the community.

Proposed Deﬁnition:

Girdwood Workforce Housing means a dwelling unit intended and maintained as a primary
residence for an individual or household in which at least one adult household member is
substantially employed or self-employed within the Girdwood Valley Service Area region.

Note: An income restriction may be speciﬁcally imposed upon a particular development,
program, funding source, or deed restriction, depending on the project.

Qualifying Local Employment:

The employee shall work a minimum of 1,400 qualifying hours per year, approximately 27 hours
per week averaged annually; OR 75% of household earned income derived from qualifying
employment or self-employment.

Note: Allowing either test could accommodate traditional employees, seasonal workers,
contractors and self-employed business owners.

Additional Local Employment Reference Points / Examples:

Entry Level – Resort

$18/hour @ 27 hours per week x 50 weeks = $24,300

Based on 30% of pre-tax income allocated to housing, this equates to monthly rent of $607.

$18/hour @ 40 hours per week x 50 weeks = $36,000 annual

Based on 30% of pre-tax income allocated to housing, this equates to monthly rent of $900.

Entry Level - Independent

$20/hour @ 27 hours per week x 50 weeks = $27,000

Based on 30% of pre-tax income allocated to housing, this equates to monthly rent of $675.

$20/hour @ 40 hours per week x 50 weeks = $40,000 annual

Based on 30% of pre-tax income allocated to housing, this equates to monthly rent of $1000.

Entry Level - Teacher

Starting Teacher Pay: $61,454 in annual salary at B00/Step 0 for the 2026-2027 school year.
Based on 30% of pre-tax income allocated to housing, this equates to monthly rent of $1,536.

Experienced Level - Teacher

Experienced Teacher Pay: $108,318 in annual salary at B72/Step 20 for the 2026-2027 school
year. Based on 30% of pre-tax income allocated to housing, this equates to monthly rent of
$2,708.
